### KAS Fleet Health Dashboard

Fleet-wide view of kube-apiserver health across all HCP clusters: **error rates** and **traffic**.

Uses pre-computed recording rules (`kas:apiserver_request_*`). Error rate = 5xx responses / total requests.

**Related dashboards**: [KAS Availability SLO](/d/fezhc0hbfefb4f/kas-api-slo) · [KAS Golden Signals](/d/hcp-kas-golden-signals/kas-golden-signals) (per-cluster drill-in)

Error-rate buckets and the fleet rate stats add the selected regional workspaces together. Each datasource is already one region. Latency panels are not on this dashboard until the latency recording rules exist.

panels.title: Error Rate Distribution — 30 Days
panels.description: Clusters in each error-rate bucket. Each selected regional workspace is counted, then the counts for the same bucket are added together.

panels.title: Error Rate Distribution — 6 Hours
panels.description: Clusters in each error-rate bucket. Each selected regional workspace is counted, then the counts for the same bucket are added together.

panels.title: Error Rate Distribution — 1 Hour
panels.description: Clusters in each error-rate bucket. Each selected regional workspace is counted, then the counts for the same bucket are added together.
Sum of kube-apiserver request rates across the selected regional workspaces.
panels.title: Fleet request rate

panels.description: Sum of kube-apiserver 5xx rates across the selected regional workspaces. A workspace with traffic and no 5xx series contributes 0.
panels.title: Fleet 5xx rate
Fleet Total Request Rate
panels.description: Request rate for each selected regional workspace. The stats beside this chart add those rates across workspaces.

Average number of requests currently being processed by the kube-apiserver (5-minute average), broken down by request kind (mutating vs read-only). High values approaching the max-inflight limit indicate the API server is close to capacity.
panels.title: In-Flight Requests (Fleet Total)

panels.description: Rate at which the kube-apiserver forcibly terminates requests because max-inflight limits are exceeded. Non-zero values mean the API server is rejecting customer traffic — this is a customer-visible outage signal.
panels.title: Request Terminations (Fleet Total)

panels.description: Top 10 clusters by the sum of mutating and read-only in-flight requests. HyperShift's default limits are 1000 mutating and 3000 read-only, 4000 combined. Yellow is 2000 and red is 3200, half and 80% of that default. A cluster that overrides those flags will not match these colors.
panels.title: Top 10 Clusters by In-Flight Saturation

panels.description: Clusters where the API server is forcibly terminating requests. Any entry here means customer traffic is being dropped on that cluster.
panels.title: Clusters with Non-Zero Terminations
